title: Acadia slides on Phase 2 miss in Alzheimer’s psychosis but keeps moving asset forward
snippet: While Acadia Pharmaceuticals’ candidate has missed the main goal of a Phase 2 trial, the company is still moving forward with the anti-psychosis candidate in Alzheimer’s disease as well as Lewy body dementia.

title: Merck’s experimental eye drug matches Roche’s VEGF inhibitor but safety concerns emerge
snippet: Analysts were keen to see a new modality compete with Roche’s approved drug Lucentis in the late-stage trial but new safety issues could complicate the future for Merck’s candidate.

title: Kyverna steps closer to FDA-first CAR T for an autoimmune condition with durability data
snippet: Kyverna Therapeutics' miv-cel showed improved mobility and a favorable safety profile at one year in patients with stiff person syndrome, further derisking an upcoming FDA application, William Blair said on Thursday. The biotech plans to file for priority review this year.

title: Eli Lilly’s weekly insulin shot cleared by FDA, setting up another front in Novo rivalry
snippet: The weekly insulin Onswik will now be available to U.S. patients after initial approvals in Europe, Mexico and Japan.

title: Backed by NVIDIA and Anthropic, Basecamp bags $140M to advance AI-designed drugs
snippet: Basecamp Research joins the growing group of AI-forward biotechs that in recent months have brought in notable sums from investors, including Isomorphic Labs and Enveda.

title: Roche inks up to $2B deal with Atavistik for new cardiometabolic drugs
snippet: The new partnership follows Roche’s recent R&D expansion in Boston focused on development for cardiovascular, renal and metabolic diseases.

title: Lilly sets aside up to $3.25B to tackle critical unmet need targets with InnoCare
snippet: InnoCare Pharma is the latest addition to Eli Lilly’s dealmaking spree, which includes some of the biggest acquisitions this year: up to $7 billion for Kelonia Therapeutics in April and up to $7.8 billion for Centessa Pharmaceuticals in March.

title: How radioligand therapy is rewriting cancer care
snippet: In this episode of Denatured presented by Curium, Jennifer Smith-Parker speaks to Mike Patterson, CEO North America and Professor Sabine Brookman-May, vice president and head of Global Clinical Development. We look at the momentum behind radioligand therapy and how its diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities are impro...

title: The human cost of AI interviews
snippet: While artificial intelligence can help biotech and pharma companies more quickly vet job applicants, it can also turn off the very people they want to employ. Two recruiting experts discuss AI’s role and limitations in the hiring process.

title: Growth mode: 3 biotechs that are staffing up after series B raises
snippet: Biotechs that announced series B financing this year and are expanding their workforces include one that raised $2.1 billion and has partnerships with Eli Lilly, Johnson & Johnson and Novartis.

title: Immunovant ditches lupus for multi-hyphenate inflammatory drug after mid-stage miss
snippet: After imeroprubart failed to demonstrate sufficient efficacy in lupus during a Phase 2b trial, Immunovant is moving on from the indication and looking to other high priority programs for the drug in neurology, endocrinology and rheumatology.

title: AI drug hunter Enveda raises $311M for late-stage obesity, inflammatory disease push
snippet: Tech darling Enveda has raised a total of $845 million in the past six years. The latest funding round is intended to pave the way for an IPO someday.

title: Amgen asset from $27.8B Horizon buy scores in Phase 3 Sjögren's study
snippet: Amgen is awaiting another Phase 3 readout for the investigational Sjögren's disease therapy, set for later this year. William Blair anticipates that at least two trials will be needed to support an FDA application.

title: Roche-Ionis’ RNA therapy reduces kidney disease marker, opening path to swift FDA nod
snippet: A late-stage test of Roche and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ sefaxersen showed that the drug reduced protein in the urine, which suggests the RNA-targeting therapy could improve kidney function and delay transplant.

title: Novo workforce down 13,000
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Novartis bets up to $900M for radioligand therapy from China’s BoomRay
snippet: Novartis is the current radiopharma leader with two FDA-approved therapies in Pluvicto and Lutathera.

title: Ionis-Otsuka offer 'groundbreaking' improvement in function and survival for genetic type of ALS
snippet: Ulefnersen, an RNA-targeted therapy being developed by Ionis Pharmaceuticals and Otsuka Pharmaceutical, improved measurements of functional impairment and survival in patients with a rare, genetic ALS subtype in a Phase 3 trial. The partners plan to approach the FDA with the results to determine potential pathways for...

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Novo’s turnaround plan, weight loss wins, Ultragenyx’s Sanfilippo approval, IPO blitz
snippet: Novo plans to hit $23B in revenue by 2035, has further reduced its workforce by 4,000 and is boosting manufacturing capacity for its Wegovy pill, but investors are unconvinced it will be enough to turn things around; Viking Therapeutics and Roche report positive results for their weight loss assets; Ultragenyx snags F...

title: Pharmas face off for manufacturing talent amidst reshoring efforts
snippet: As pharmas reshore manufacturing, they’re squaring off with each other to find the right personnel to staff up their plants. That task is challenging given the limited talent pool, difficulty filling critical roles and, in some cases, competition from data centers.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.
